Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

In the provided extracted text, there is no evidence of install-time automatic execution via .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious setup.py logic, abused PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects.

The if __name__ == "__main__": blocks in pbest/main.py and pbest/containerization/containerization_cli.py appear to be normal user-invoked script/CLI paths, not malicious supply-chain auto-execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential theft: No evidence of broad environment-variable harvesting, .env discovery, SSH key collection, cloud/CI token collection, wallet theft, or registry token discovery. The PYPI_TOKEN use in publish.sh appears to be normal token handling for a user-run release publishing script.
  • Exfiltration/staging: ZIP/OMEX creation/extraction and remote simulation submission to compose.cam.uchc.edu are present, but they appear tied to the package’s experiment-archive and explicit remote-execution functionality. There is no evidence connecting them to secret harvesting, stealth, or attacker-controlled C2 exfiltration.
  • Persistence: No evidence of cron jobs, systemd units, launch agents, shell-profile modification, or self-reinstall loops.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence of Kubernetes service-account abuse, Docker socket theft, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection.
  • Stealth/loaders: No evidence of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec-based loaders, obfuscated downloader stubs, or self-deleting droppers. The pre-scan’s base64-like matches appear to be hashes/URLs inside uv.lock.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

Based on the provided material, there is no evidence of malicious extra files in the PyPI artifact, hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting, sudden dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch.

tests/resources/simulators/copasi_phase_cycle.omex was flagged as a high-entropy binary/archive, but OMEX is an expected test-resource format for this package’s domain. The available evidence is insufficient to classify it as a malicious payload.

Further Verification Needed

  • The review was primarily based on the 28 files included in the text corpus out of 66 extracted files; unprovided files should be checked separately for automatic execution hooks.
  • Only the sdist was provided; no wheel comparison was available, so wheel/sdist mismatch could not be assessed.
  • The .omex test archive contents were not fully expanded in the static text corpus; further manual inspection may be needed for complete assurance.
